text: January 14, 2026 - Kusunda is a critically endangered language isolate spoken by a small ethnic group of the same name in the mid-western and central regions of Nepal, including districts such as Dang, Surkhet, Pyuthan, Gorkha, Tanahu, and Rolpa.[1] As of 2025, it has only one fluent native speaker, 50-year-old Kamala Sen Kusunda (born 1975), following the death of the previous last fluent speaker, Gyani Maiya Sen, in 2020; approximately 150 to 253 individuals identify ethnically as Kusunda, but most speak Nepali as their primary language due to historical marginalization and language shift.[2][3] First document
